title: Nominations open for South Carolina's Emerging Leaders Under 40 until July 31
text:
Nominations open for South Carolina’s Emerging Leaders Under 40 until July 31
Employers, colleagues, mentors and community leaders have until July 31 to nominate candidates for the Emerging Leaders Under 40 program in South Carolina, according to SCBIZ on July 15. The statewide recognition program continues the legacy of Forty Under 40 by honoring professionals under the age of 40 whose leadership, innovation and community involvement are shaping the state’s future.
Emerging Leaders Under 40 was created following the launch of SCBIZ as a unified statewide business media brand. The new format aims to recognize young professionals from across South Carolina and expand opportunities to celebrate those driving innovation, growing businesses and serving their communities. “We didn’t want to leave behind the legacy of Forty Under 40—we wanted to build on it,” said Ben Jacobs, Content Lead at SCBIZ. “Emerging Leaders Under 40 carries forward everything that made Forty Under 40 meaningful while creating a statewide platform that reflects where South Carolina’s business community is today.”
Jacobs said, “Every organization has someone who is making an extraordinary impact. Too often, those individuals aren’t recognized because everyone assumes someone else will nominate them. As the nomination deadline approaches, we encourage business leaders across South Carolina to take a few minutes to recognize the emerging leaders within their organizations and communities.”
Eligible nominees must be employed in South Carolina, be age 39 or younger by the eligibility deadline, demonstrate exceptional professional achievement and show commitment to community service. Previous recipients of Forty Under 40 are not eligible for this honor.
Key dates include a nomination deadline on July 31; application deadline on August 14; and an honoree celebration scheduled for October 20 at Columbia Metropolitan Convention Center in Columbia.
The Charleston Metro Chamber of Commerce supports talent development initiatives designed to bolster regional economic growth through advocacy, leadership programs and member services; it serves businesses throughout Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester counties while offering networking opportunities and educational resources, according to its official website.
